text:
maria-sales: FYI — HealthNode (gov healthcare customer) wants a 4-week POC. Ask: suggested reserved GPU commit, autoscale template, KMS options, and whether we can accept a strict latency SLA for certain routes. Workload: conversational chat + vector search. Steady ~140 rps, intermittent regional spikes to 900 rps (~8-12m). Avg request ~160 tokens. They require VPC peering, SOC2 docs, and prefer customer-managed keys if possible. Any blockers?

yasmin-solutions: Nice lead. Do we know if spikes align to business hours or are unpredictable? Also need expected concurrency per session to size KV warmup.

maria-sales: Spikes are mostly East US business hours. Concurrency ~1.1k concurrent sessions peak.

rachel-runtime: Quick guidance: with q4 quant we get ~280 rps/GPU for this profile. For steady 140 rps you can do 2 reserved GPUs minimal, but given SLA desire and spikes I recommend 5 reserved GPUs + autoscale to 15 for burst headroom. Lock model+quant in the offer (e.g., redwood-clarity-1.2 + q4_0).

tony-sre: Ops notes: AZ spread required (min 2 per AZ), warm KV preheat run before business hours, and queue-depth alerts. Sample autoscale snippet we give presales: 
```yaml
autoscale_policy:
  min_replicas: "1"
  reserved_replicas: "5"
  max_replicas: "15"
  target_rps_per_gpu: "280"
  preheat_window: "6m"
  cooldown: "90s"
  az_spread: "true"
```

yasmin-solutions: For the POC we usually include a capped burst-credit pool (recommend 6k burst-minutes) and a 72hr smoke run against a golden prompt set mid-POC to validate tail latency. We will supply runbook and load scripts.

kevin-pricing: Pricing: 5 reserved GPUs baseline + on-demand billing for burst beyond credits. If they want customer-managed KMS during the POC, that’s an enterprise add-on (longer lead + setup fee). Ill prepare two quote lines: standard POC and POC-with-CMK. Need estimate of monthly burst minutes to finalize numbers.

emma-security: SOC2 docs OK to share. For KMS: customer-managed keys require Dedicated/Private deployment and an additional security review. For POC we can provide sanitized audit logs and a KMS escrow option (short-term) but CMK in their tenant requires more time. Also need their IP allowlist and dataflow approvals.

maria-sales: Legal asked if we can promise 25ms 50p for search routes and 100ms 50p for chat during steady-state. Realistic?

rachel-runtime: 25ms 50p for vector search is extremely aggressive at this size unless we use a distilled embedding model or local cache tier. Recommend: embeddings/search 50p <80ms (with reserved commit and caching), chat 50p <250ms as our POC target. If they insist on 25ms we should offer a premium SLA with distilled model + higher reserved commit and priority routing.

kevin-pricing: If premium SLA desired, reserved commit will need to increase (estimate 2x) and add priority scheduling fee (~+70%). Ill build pricing scenarios: standard, CMK add-on, premium-latency.

tony-sre: Operational blockers to call out in the quote: IP allowlist for VPC peering, approval for cross-AZ preheat traffic, golden-prompt set to validate tail latency, and acceptance of our fallback policy (we can divert heavy requests to smaller model during overload).

yasmin-solutions: Ill draft a POC runbook and the warmup script. Also include a short test plan: daily preheat, mid-POC 72hr smoke, and acceptance criteria (tail latency thresholds + error rate).

infra-bot: presales-smokejob queued: healthnode_poc_2026-08-09. ETA 12m.

maria-sales: Next steps: 1) Ill ask customer for CIDRs and confirm spike cadence, 2) kevin will attach pricing scenarios, 3) emma will attach SOC2 + KMS timeline note, 4) yasmin + tony will run sandbox smoke and share runbook. Tagging: @yasmin-solutions @tony-sre @kevin-pricing @emma-security.

emma-security: Ill also include a short checklist they can return with the questionnaire (CIDRs, required retention period, CMK intent).

kevin-pricing: Got it — will post draft lines by EOD.

maria-sales: Thanks team — will update HealthNode and loop back. :thumbsup:
